correct_completion: the children went back to their classes.
full_sentence: Lunch finished, the children went back to their classes.
acceptable_variants: the children lined up at the door.

options.why_wrong: This describes a state, but the stem sets up a sequence of events. After lunch ends, the next event is returning to class.

options.text: the children went back to their classes.

options.why_wrong: This refers to a past meal, which does not follow the end of the lunch described in the stem.

options.text: the lunch menu was very long.
options.why_wrong: This describes the menu, not an event that follows the end of lunch.

grammar_focus: Absolute clause (noun plus past participle) followed by a main clause
explanation: The absolute clause 'Lunch finished' gives the time of the main action without a conjunction, so the main clause must describe what happens next. Spanish speakers may try to add a conjunction or a verb to the absolute clause, but English uses a noun followed by a past participle with no verb 'to be'.
translation: Terminó el almuerzo, y los niños volvieron a sus clases.
